objectives.title: Open a page in the live browser
objectives.why: Everything else — clicking, tracing, debugging — starts from a page the agent actually opened and can see.

objectives.title: Take a snapshot before interacting with the page
objectives.why: A snapshot gives you stable element references (uids) to click and fill by — the alternative is guessing coordinates.

objectives.title: Drive the page — click, fill, or submit a form
objectives.why: Automating real interaction is what turns this from a screenshot tool into a testing tool.

objectives.title: Handle a browser dialog instead of getting stuck on it
objectives.why: An unhandled alert or confirm() blocks every tool after it until something responds.

objectives.title: Check the console for errors
objectives.why: Half of what's wrong with a page never reaches the DOM — it's sitting in the console.

objectives.title: Inspect a network request
objectives.why: Seeing the actual request/response beats guessing why an API call failed.

objectives.title: Evaluate a script against the live page
objectives.why: Sometimes the fastest way to check a value is to just ask the page for it.

objectives.title: Capture a screenshot
objectives.why: A screenshot is proof of what actually rendered, not what you expected to render.

objectives.title: Emulate a device or network condition
objectives.why: Most bugs users report only show up on a slower network or a smaller viewport — reproduce the condition instead of guessing.

objectives.title: Record a performance trace
objectives.why: A trace shows you where the time actually went instead of where you assumed it went.

objectives.title: Pull an optimization insight out of a trace
objectives.why: A recorded trace is just data until something extracts what's actually slow.

objectives.title: Run a Lighthouse audit
objectives.why: Lighthouse turns 'is this page fast enough?' into a scored, comparable answer.

objectives.title: Take a heap snapshot
objectives.why: A heap snapshot is the only way to see what's actually holding memory instead of guessing at a leak.

objectives.title: Compare two heap snapshots to find a leak
objectives.why: A single snapshot shows a moment; comparing two shows what's growing between them.

objectives.title: Work across multiple tabs
objectives.why: Real flows — OAuth popups, opening a link in a new tab — need more than one page open at once.

objectives.title: Load and test a Chrome extension
objectives.why: Testing an extension for real means loading it into a real browser, not just reading its manifest.

bestPractices.title: Close the pages you open
bestPractices.why: Every new_page leaves a browser tab running until something closes it — over a long session that's a pile of stale tabs holding memory and connections open.

bestPractices.title: Release a heap snapshot once you're done with it
bestPractices.why: A heap snapshot is held in memory until closed — forgetting to close it defeats the point of freeing memory up to look for a leak.
